issue.title: Three test modules import the deleted sase.ace.tui.proc_queue and only survive via a tests/ace/tui/conftest.py stub, so they fail to collect in a scoped run
issue.description:
Found by the sase-q0 land agent while verifying that epic; originally proposed as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on phase bead sase-q0.1.

`src/sase/ace/tui/proc_queue.py` was deleted in 8c4840458 ("feat(ace): observe durable procs read-only", bead sase-m9.3.1.4, plan 202608/readonly_ace_proc_observer.md). Three test modules still import from it:

- `tests/_agent_cleanup_proc_helpers.py:25` — `from sase.ace.tui.proc_queue import ProcInfo`
- `tests/_plan_approval_tui_helpers.py:11` — same import
- `tests/ace/tui/test_agent_cleanup_procs.py:24` — `from sase.ace.tui.proc_queue import ProcInfo, ProcQueue`

They only work because `tests/ace/tui/conftest.py:129-134` builds a fake module and does `sys.modules.setdefault("sase.ace.tui.proc_queue", _proc_queue_module)`. That conftest is only loaded when something under `tests/ace/tui/` is part of the collection, so importability of those three modules depends on collection ORDER and on which directories the run happens to include.

Why this matters beyond tidiness: `just check`'s diff-scoped lane (`tools/select_tests`) picks a subset of test files from the import-graph closure of the diff. A diff touching only `src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_dismiss_persistence.py` can select `tests/test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py` without anything under `tests/ace/tui/`, and the whole scoped run then dies at collection with `ModuleNotFoundError`, not with a real test failure. Epic sase-q0's own phase sase-q0.1 modified exactly that source file and that test file.

The full suite is currently green because `tests/ace/tui/` is always collected there, which is precisely what makes this hard to notice.

SUGGESTED FIX (judgment needed): point the three test modules at the real post-migration types (`sase.ace.tui._proc_observer_models` / whatever now owns `ProcInfo`/`ProcQueue`), then delete the `sys.modules.setdefault` compat shim from `tests/ace/tui/conftest.py`. Alternatively move the shim to the top-level `tests/conftest.py` if the compat surface is still wanted — but that keeps a fake module for a deleted API, so retiring it is preferable.

task_type_fields.impact: Any diff-scoped just check run that selects tests/test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py (or the other two modules) without also selecting tests/ace/tui/ dies at collection with ModuleNotFoundError instead of running the tests. The full suite hides it because tests/ace/tui/ is always collected there.
task_type_fields.repro:
From a clean tree at master 716e9de98, after `just install`:

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py -q -p no:randomly
tests/test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py:13: in <module>
    from tests._agent_cleanup_proc_helpers import run_tracked_proc
tests/_agent_cleanup_proc_helpers.py:25: in <module>
    from sase.ace.tui.proc_queue import ProcInfo
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sase.ace.tui.proc_queue'
ERROR tests/test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py
!!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!!
```

Adding any `tests/ace/tui/` node to the same invocation makes it pass, which shows the dependency on the conftest stub:

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py tests/ace/tui/test_agent_cleanup_procs.py --collect-only -q -p no:randomly
17 tests collected
```

`.venv/bin/python -c "import sase.ace.tui.proc_queue"` also fails, and `ls src/sase/ace/tui/ | grep proc` shows no `proc_queue.py`.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-q0.1 — that phase modified both src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_dismiss_persistence.py and tests/test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py, which is how the collection error was first noticed. RELATED: sase-m9.3.1.4 — the commit (8c4840458) that deleted src/sase/ace/tui/proc_queue.py and left the conftest compat stub behind.

evidence.note:
Independently reproduced in workspace sase_17 at HEAD a67ba351f while landing epic sase-qt, and the blast radius is larger than 'three test modules': 14 top-level modules fail to collect with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sase.ace.tui.proc_queue' whenever tests/ace is not collected in the same run.

FULL LIST (14): tests/test_agent_dismiss_artifact_cleanup.py, test_agent_dismiss_in_memory.py, test_agent_dismiss_names.py, test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py, test_agent_kill_bulk.py, test_agent_kill_dismiss_fast_path.py, test_agent_kill_phase1_async_io.py, test_agent_kill_phase2_kill_all.py, test_agent_kill_single_execution.py, test_agent_kill_single_persistence.py, test_agent_launch_validation.py, test_dismissed_agent_lifecycle.py, test_plan_rejection_response.py, test_tui_plan_epic_approval.py.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED: they import tests/_agent_cleanup_proc_helpers.py, whose line 25 does 'from sase.ace.tui.proc_queue import ProcInfo'. That module no longer exists; the only thing that makes it importable is tests/ace/tui/conftest.py:129-134, which builds a types.ModuleType('sase.ace.tui.proc_queue') and sys.modules.setdefault()s it. So the helper depends on an unrelated subtree's conftest having been imported first.

REPRO: 'just test tests --ignore=tests/ace <other dirs>' -> 19142 passed, 14 errors. Rerunning the same 14 modules with a single tests/ace/tui path appended -> 138 passed in 7.99s. That is the whole difference.

IMPACT beyond the scoped-run case in the description: it also makes any directory-sliced full-suite run red, which is how a land agent verifies an epic when the suite gate reclaims a single long check-full hold.
